# Results — Study 40 (Paper-Tiger): a published dual-momentum, mirrored back

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Monthly total-return prices for **SPY
(US), EFA (foreign), AGG (bonds)** plus the **^IRX 13-week T-bill** cash hurdle (Yahoo), 2003-09 →
2026-05 (the in-progress month is dropped — the tape ends at the last completed month-end). The
strategy is Antonacci's **Global Equities Momentum** (relative momentum between US and foreign
equity, gated by an absolute-momentum T-bill filter into bonds), rebalanced monthly, **20 bp per
switch**. The offline core proves the machinery on a seeded synthetic world; this is the measurement
on the market. As-of **2026-05-31**; match the fingerprint below.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `WEAK` · Tradability `FRAGILE` · "Beats the market"? `NOT SUPPORTED`

The vendor (paperswithbacktest, *"Momentum Asset Allocation"*, SSRN 1585517 = Antonacci) sells a
headline backtest and a Sharpe. Rebuilt faithfully on real ETFs, the book reliably makes money — but
so does anything that holds equities for 23 years. The test that isolates the *timing* skill is the
**spanning regression of GEM on its own ingredients** (SPY/AGG, excess-of-cash on both sides), and
there the alpha is **+10 bp/month (≈1.2%/yr) with a HAC t of 0.49** — statistically indistinguishable
from zero. The t≈3.5 the raw mean carries is the equity premium's t-stat, not the strategy's: plain
SPY clears the same bar (Lo t **3.1** on excess) with a *higher* excess Sharpe (**0.67** vs GEM's
**0.62**). So the signal is `WEAK`: a real return stream whose statistical significance belongs to
the assets it holds, not to the switching rule. The *claim that sells it* — beats buy-and-hold — is
`NOT SUPPORTED` in either Sharpe convention, and what's genuinely distinctive is one-dimensional:
**crash protection** (max drawdown **−23%** vs SPY's **−51%**, because the filter sits in bonds
through 2008). That single dimension is `FRAGILE`: it rests on essentially **one** independent crisis
in the sample, it has **decayed since publication** (excess Sharpe 0.74 → 0.52), and as a portfolio
sleeve it leaves a 60/40's Sharpe essentially flat (0.68 → 0.70 excess) while trimming drawdown. A
sensible defensive rule; a paper-tiger headline.

## Data stamp

- **Universe**: SPY / EFA / AGG + ^IRX, 2003-09-30 → 2026-05-31, **260 invested months**, 35 switches,
  inputs fingerprint `c055e32230e2`

## GEM vs the benchmarks that actually matter — both Sharpe conventions

A raw Sharpe on an always-invested book silently includes the cash rate; an excess-of-cash Sharpe is
the convention the literature (and the Lo t-stat) actually speaks. We report both — compare raw with
raw, or excess with excess, never one of each.

| | Sharpe (raw) | Sharpe (excess of ^IRX) | CAGR | vol | max-DD | skew |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **GEM (net, 20 bp/switch)** | 0.76 | **0.62** | 9.1% | 12.5% | **−23%** | −0.40 |
| GEM (gross) | 0.79 | 0.64 | 9.4% | 12.5% | −23% | −0.40 |
| Buy & Hold SPY | 0.79 | **0.67** | 11.3% | 15.0% | −51% | −0.51 |
| 60/40 SPY/AGG (monthly rebalanced) | **0.87** | **0.68** | 8.2% | 9.6% | −32% | −0.56 |

In *both* conventions GEM does **not** beat just holding SPY, and it **loses to a plain 60/40**. The
"beats the market" headline is the paper tiger. (Note the vendor's own listed Sharpe for this idea is
`0.321` — *lower* than our 0.76; their figure is on a different universe/period. The point isn't that
their number is inflated, it's that **no** version of the number beats the right benchmark.)

## Is the *signal* real? The spanning test says no alpha

A t-test on the book's own mean cannot answer "is dual momentum skill?" — an always-invested
equity/bond book passes it in any sample where the equity premium showed up. The right test regresses
GEM's excess return on the excess returns of its own ingredients and asks whether the intercept — the
return the *switching* added that a fixed mix could not have earned — clears zero:

| spanning regression (HAC/Newey-West intercept) | alpha | t | betas | R² |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GEM net on SPY + AGG | +10 bp/mo (≈1.2%/yr) | **0.49** | 0.64 SPY / 0.08 AGG | 0.60 |
| GEM net on the 60/40 | +10 bp/mo | **0.48** | 0.99 | 0.59 |

For the record, the book-level numbers in both conventions: excess-of-cash Lo t **2.84**, HAC mean
**64 bp/mo** t **2.94** — but plain SPY posts Lo t **3.08** on the same footing (raw: Lo t 3.50, HAC
t 3.61). The book's mean is solidly positive; the *timing alpha* is statistically zero. That is what
`WEAK` means here: significant as a return stream, not significant as a strategy.

## What's actually distinctive: crash protection (and only that)

| | GEM | SPY |
|---|---|---|
| mean return in the worst-decile SPY months (n = 26) | **−4.97%/mo** | −7.74%/mo |
| correlation to SPY *in those months* | **−0.01** | — |

In the months that hurt, GEM bleeds ~2.8 pts/month less than the index and is essentially uncorrelated
to it — the absolute-momentum filter is in bonds. That cushion is the entire edge.

## Why the cushion is `FRAGILE`, not `INVESTABLE`

1. **One crisis does the work.** Over 2003–2026 there is really one deep equity bear (2008) plus
   shallow ones (2020, 2022). The drawdown advantage is concentrated in a handful of months — a thin
   independent-observation count behind an impressive-looking 23-year chart.
2. **Post-publication decay.** Sub-period Sharpe (raw / excess): **2004–2013 0.87 / 0.74** →
   **2014–2026 0.68 / 0.52**. Antonacci published dual momentum in 2012–14; the edge is softer since
   (cf. McLean & Pontiff 2016).
3. **It barely moves a portfolio's Sharpe.** Blending a 30% GEM sleeve into a 60/40 nudges the excess
   Sharpe **0.68 → 0.70** while cutting max-DD **−32% → −27%** — a drawdown trim, not a return engine.
   Unlike a genuinely decorrelated sleeve (cf. study 31's trend book), GEM mostly buys you a little
   less drawdown — and a 60/40 you already own gives more Sharpe for less effort.

## The honest takeaway

Dual momentum is a **sensible, low-turnover** crash-defensive rule — far from a fraud. But its
statistical case dissolves under the right test: the raw t≈3.5 certifies the equity-and-bond premium
the book carries, not the switching rule (spanning alpha t **0.49**), it ties or trails buy-and-hold
and loses to 60/40 on Sharpe in both conventions, its one real gift (shallower drawdowns) leans on one
crisis and has faded since publication, and it adds almost no risk-adjusted return to a portfolio
you'd plausibly already hold. `WEAK` signal, `FRAGILE` standalone, `NOT SUPPORTED` as a market-beater —
which is a very different study from the one the headline Sharpe advertises.
